title: Assessments, Consultations and Consideration of Alternative Sites for Housing before Decisions on Clearance of Gillman Barracks and Maju Forest
what_it_is: Assessments, Consultations and Consideration of Alternative Sites for Housing before Decisions on Clearance of Gillman Barracks and Maju Forest

sections.label: Gillman Barracks housing site questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether alternative sites, smaller-footprint options and clearance checkpoints were assessed for Gillman Barracks housing, and whether dialogue sessions will follow the feedback period.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether alternative sites for housing were evaluated as alternatives to Gillman Barracks; (b) whether smaller-footprint or lower-density options on the Gillman Barracks site itself, with greater retention of forest cover and heritage buildings, were also assessed against the current conceptual plan; and (c) what planning considerations led to the proposed site and footprint being preferred.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development whether, after the online feedback period for the Gillman Barracks Environmental Impact Assessment and Heritage Impact Assessment closes on 6 August 2026, the Government will hold dialogue sessions with residents, heritage groups and nature groups as part of the process of refining the development plans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the phased directional clearance plan for Gillman Barracks under the Environmental Monitoring and Management Plan will include checkpoints at which monitoring data from earlier phases is reviewed before authorising further clearance; and (b) if so, what criteria would trigger a pause or adjustment to the clearance schedule.

sections.label: Biodiversity harm threshold questions
sections.summary: Questions ask what harm threshold sets a site aside and whether under-used state land was assessed as an alternative before clearance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development given that the Environmental Impact Assessments at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks rate the biodiversity impact as major negative after mitigation (a) what threshold of harm sets a site aside if that finding does not; and (b) whether under-used state land, including the grounds of black-and-white bungalows and ageing low-rise estates, has been assessed as an alternative before clearance.

sections.label: Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks impacts
sections.summary: Questions ask about climate impacts, brownfield alternatives, clearing costs and whether HDB will publish housing demand and site selection reasoning before consultations close.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in relation to the Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks redevelopments (a) what is the impact on surface temperature and greenhouse gas emissions; (b) whether brownfield alternatives were surveyed and what is the rationale for selecting these sites; (c) what is the estimated cost of clearing Maju Forest versus redeveloping a similar area in mature estates; and (d) whether Environmental Impact Assessments measure climate-related factors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development whether HDB will publish, before consultations on the Sunset Way and Gillman Barracks sites close on 6 August 2026 (i) the projected housing demand these sites are intended to meet and (ii) the reasoning for selecting them over available alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The plans for Gillman Barracks and Sunset Way have not been finalised.

sections.label: Consultation and continued engagement
sections.summary: Studies and conceptual plans were published for public views, and engagement will continue after the formal consultation period ends on 6 August 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We published the studies and conceptual plans so the public can study them, share their views and help us to shape the final development plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I want to assure Members that while the formal consultation period for the Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) and Heritage Impact Assessment (HIA) ends on 6 August 2026, our engagement with stakeholders will continue, as we adjust and refine the development plans based on the inputs received.

sections.label: Golf course land redevelopment
sections.summary: By 2030, more than 400 hectares of golf course land will have been taken back for redevelopment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: By 2030, we will have taken back more than 400 hectares of golf course land for redevelopment.

sections.label: Safeguarded green space
sections.summary: Even after accounting for planned developments in the latest Master Plan, URA has safeguarded an additional 1,000 hectares of green space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Even after accounting for planned developments in the latest Master Plan, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) has safeguarded an additional 1,000 hectares of green space.

sections.label: Sunset Way housing planning intention
sections.summary: The planning intention for housing at Sunset Way has been in the Master Plan since 1980 and was reaffirmed in the 2025 review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For Sunset Way, the planning intention for housing had been reflected in the Master Plan since 1980.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That intention has been reviewed and reaffirmed at each subsequent Master Plan review, including the most recent review in 2025.

sections.label: Clementi BTO launches oversubscribed
sections.summary: The recent BTO launches at Clementi Emerald and Berlayar Rise were each oversubscribed by over four times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The recent BTO launches at Clementi Emerald and Berlayar Rise were each oversubscribed by over four times.

sections.label: Redevelopment and LTA worksite
sections.summary: The former will be redeveloped for public and private housing, and the latter is an LTA worksite for the Cross Island Line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The former will be redeveloped for a mix of public and private housing, to be launched over the next few years, and the latter is a Land Transport Authority (LTA) worksite that is needed to support ongoing works for the Cross Island Line.

sections.label: Gillman Barracks forest retention study
sections.summary: At Gillman Barracks, the government is studying how to retain most of the native-dominated secondary forest within the site.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: At Gillman Barracks, we are studying how to retain most of the native-dominated secondary forest within the site.

sections.label: Gillman Barracks heritage building retention
sections.summary: At Gillman Barracks, the government is studying retention of all buildings of Exceptional heritage significance and most of High significance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Gillman Barracks also has a distinctive heritage character.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We are thus studying the retention of all buildings assessed to be of "Exceptional" heritage significance, as well as most of those assessed to be of "High" heritage significance.

sections.label: Sunset Way greenery retention study
sections.summary: At Sunset Way, the government is studying the retention of a significant stretch of greenery along the former Jurong Railway Line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: At Sunset Way, we are studying the retention of a significant stretch of greenery along the former Jurong Railway Line.

sections.label: Post-consultation engagement and review
sections.summary: After consultation closes on 6 August 2026, further stakeholder engagements and review of findings and feedback will precede finalising development plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: After the formal consultation period closes on 6 August 2026, we will conduct further engagements with stakeholders and closely review the study findings and feedback we received before finalising our detailed development plans.

sections.label: Leaving a greener country
sections.summary: The responsibility is to leave children a greener, more liveable country that continues to provide opportunities and good homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Our responsibility is to do the same – so that we can leave to our children a country that is greener, more liveable and continues to provide opportunities and good homes for our people.

sections.label: Plans not finalised, further engagement
sections.summary: Sunset Way and Gillman Barracks plans are not finalised; engagement continues after 6 August, then reports on feedback responses and plan adjustments will be released.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier on, the plans for both Sunset Way, and in this case, Gillman Barracks are not yet finalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Even beyond 6 August, when the consultation period closes, we will continue to engage her residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And after this further engagement and reviewing the feedback and findings from additional engagements with the residents, we will release reports summarising the responses to feedback and also any adjustments that we make to the original set of plans.

sections.label: Proposed ecological corridors
sections.summary: Both studies proposed a minimum 30-metre ecological corridor, and for Gillman Barracks the recommended corridor stretches up to 200 metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Both studies also proposed a minimum 30-metre ecological corridor, and for Gillman Barracks, its recommended corridor stretches up to 200 metres.

sections.label: Green space and safeguarded hectares
sections.summary: Singapore has over 7,800 hectares of green spaces and nature reserves, and URA safeguarded an additional 1,000 hectares of green space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On the spaces which the Member has mentioned, as I have mentioned, today, Singapore has over 7,800 hectares of green spaces and nature reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And if you look at the bigger picture, even after accounting for the planned developments in both sites in the Master Plan, URA has safeguarded an additional 1,000 hectares of green space.

sections.label: MRT planning and sensitive sites
sections.summary: The question asks whether MRT planning will consider sensitive ecological sites like Maju Forest; the reply says Sunset Way and Gillman Barracks are zoned for housing and EIAs and HIAs will guide mitigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And if that being the case, will the Government consider in the future, when planning MRT lines, alignments and station locations, that we take into account the location of sensitive, ecological sites, such as Maju Forest, such that we do not perpetuate a vicious cycle where this station is planned for that location and therefore, it compels development of the forest?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I made it quite clear that the sites that we mentioned earlier on – Sunset Way as well as Gillman Barracks – have already been zoned for residential use under our Master Plan and they have been set aside for housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, we will proceed, but how we build is important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And that is why we have these EIAs and HIA to identify the ecological significance, the heritage significance, and then, we will mitigate as best as possible, the ecological and heritage impact to the sites.

sections.label: Ecological profiling and impact assessments
sections.summary: An ecological profiling exercise is done on a broad swath, and EIA and HIA are used to mitigate sites meant for development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Number one, we do an ecological profiling exercise on a broad swath to look at the impact of where sites have ecological and natural heritage, natural significance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Then, when the sites are meant to be developed, we also look at the EIA and the HIA to mitigate those sites.

sections.label: Planning permission and environmental screening
sections.summary: No development can take place without planning permission, and all development proposals are screened for environmental and heritage impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The first is that no development can take place without planning permission under the Planning Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And as part of the planning approval process, all development proposals are screened for potential environmental as well as heritage impact.

sections.label: Alternative sites and Clementi Avenue 5
sections.summary: Land use is optimised and vacant and brownfield sites tapped, but no other suitable sites meet near-term demand; Clementi Avenue 5 supports Cross Island Line works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier on the alternative sites, and I thank Mr Christopher de Souza for being very practical and also identifying some potential alternative sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We do our best to optimise the land use and to tap the vacant land and brownfield sites where possible, but there are no other suitable sites to meet the near-turn demand in the vicinity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Clementi Avenue 5 is also to support ongoing works for the Cross Island Line, but will be considered for residential development after the MRT line is complete.

sections.label: Extended engagement and published responses
sections.summary: Engagements will be extended beyond 6 August, views and feedback will be considered in finalising plans, and agencies' responses will be published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: First, we will be extending the engagements beyond 6 August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, as I have mentioned, please share with us your views and your feedback, and we will take them into consideration as we finalise the plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We will also publish the agencies' responses to this feedback.

sections.label: Clementi Emerald oversubscription
sections.summary: Clementi Emerald is four times oversubscribed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: At close by, Clementi Emerald, for example, is four times oversubscribed.

sections.label: Protective Security Command and brownfield sites
sections.summary: The Protective Security Command is set aside for residential housing, and surrounding brownfield sites have been looked at before vegetated sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I think the Protective Security Command is also set aside for residential housing, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And as I mentioned, also to Mr Christopher de Souza, we have already looked at all of the surrounding brownfield sites and where possible, we have to factor in the timing, the availability, the infrastructure, as well as the lease and other factors before we go into vegetated sites.

sections.label: Major negative EIA term
sections.summary: A major negative is a formal EIA technical term, and ecological and heritage impacts cannot always be avoided, including at Sunset Way and Gillman Barracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: A "major negative" is a formal technical term used in the EIA and it is not always possible to avoid the ecological and heritage impact, including the type for Sunset Way and Gillman Barracks.

sections.label: Engagements extended beyond consultation
sections.summary: Engagements and consultation will be extended beyond the consultation period on 6 August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On the engagements and the consultation, I also mentioned that we will extend it beyond the consultation period on 6 August.

sections.label: MSE and MND positions
sections.summary: The suggestion that MSE should take a different position from MND and object to MND decisions is not how the government works.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The suggestion that MSE should take on a different position than MND, and to make a strong stance because it is the Year of Climate Adaptation, to object to some of the decisions that have been taken by MND – it is not how we work as a government.

sections.label: Request for MND report
sections.summary: Questions remain on why high ecological value areas are excluded and how the decision was reached, so MND is asked to publish a report.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Questions remain, such as why more areas of high ecological value are not included within the proposed retained area, and they want to know how the decision was reached and whether every reasonable alternative has been considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Hence, my second supplementary question is, will MND publish a report similar to the National Climate Change Secretariat's response on Singapore's long-term low emissions development strategy to respond to these questions and suggestions, and explain how feedback informed its final decision?

sections.label: Studying green space retention
sections.summary: The study covers retention of green spaces including greenery along the former Old Jurong Railway Line, a natural stream and a riparian buffer, and a report will be published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: If you look at what we are trying to study, we are trying to study the retention of some of these green spaces, including a significant stretch of greenery along the former Old Jurong Railway Line, also a natural stream and a riparian buffer that will help to support wildlife.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And we will also publish a report summarising the agencies' responses to feedback and also any amendments made to the original plans.

sections.label: Medway Park bungalow redevelopment
sections.summary: In coming years, plans to redevelop bungalows at Medway Park as part of the Dover-Medway Estate will be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In the coming years, we will also be studying plans to redevelop bungalows at Medway Park as part of the Dover-Medway Estate.

sections.label: Liveable city and greenery conserved
sections.summary: Singapore is one of the most liveable cities and has conserved over 7,800 hectares of greenery despite limited space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, overall, if we look at where we are as a nation, we are one of the most liveable cities in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And despite our limited space, we have gone on to conserve and preserve over 7,800 hectares of greenery, within all of these constraints.

sections.label: Gillman Barracks and Maju Forest housing
sections.summary: The member asks whether 7,000 units near Southern Waterfront and 20,000 units near Maju Forest are not enough.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first being that we are talking about Gillman Barracks and also, Maju Forest.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I noticed and I believe the Minister of State also said earlier that the Southern Waterfront, for example, is an area that is being developed, and I believe that the numbers is estimated about 7,000 new units, and nearer to Maju Forest, we have got a Turf City development, where up to 20,000 housing units are being proposed, or at least being planned.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask, despite all these numbers coming up, is it actually the Government's or at least MND's assessment that these 7,000, 20,000 units coming up in the vicinity is not enough?

sections.label: Residents want housing in central areas
sections.summary: Residents with multiple ballots cannot get homes and demand for housing in central areas is four times oversubscribed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I definitely face my residents saying, "I have multiple ballots and I can't get the home." And residents and homeowners want housing, they want housing, many of them want housing in central areas living near their parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And that is why the demand for housing in these areas are now, four times oversubscribed, as I mentioned in my earlier reply.

sections.label: Brownfield sites before vegetated sites
sections.summary: The Government will continue to look for alternatives and focus on brownfield sites and vacant land before touching vegetated sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Yes, we have and we will continue to look for alternatives and focus on brownfield sites and vacant land before we touch a vegetated site.

sections.label: Firm and non-firm housing sites
sections.summary: Master Plan housing sites like Newton are firm, while Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks are not firm and have a consultation period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The first is on the sites in the Master Plan with housing use, I think she mentioned Newton and other places, it is because the plans are firm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For Maju Forest and for Gillman Barracks, they are not firm and that is why we have the consultation period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And I mentioned earlier on that we make adjustments already prior with the EIA and HIA, where we could potentially have built more homes for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But we already have the EIA and HIA where we already accept that there will be lesser homes and the feedback exercise that will go beyond 6 August, as Speaker had mentioned, I have explained many times, will continue to help us to shape these plans as we go ahead.

sections.label: SLA engaged Gillman Barracks tenants
sections.summary: SLA has engaged Gillman Barracks tenants since 2023 and informed them the site is safeguarded for residential use in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Singapore Land Authority (SLA) has already engaged tenants at Gillman Barracks since 2023 and informed that the site has already been safeguarded for residential use in the longer term.

sections.label: Children's placard to save forest
sections.summary: A Member says David Hoe messaged him at 2.30 am after his Meet-the-People Session, showing two young children with a placard reading "Please save the forest."

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Earlier this morning, at 2.30 am, as I was preparing for this, Mr David Hoe messaged me and he said he just finished his Meet-the-People Session, and he showed me two young children with a little placard and it says, "Please save the forest." I texted him and I said, "That is wonderful".

sections.label: Building homes in heritage estates
sections.summary: A Member says homes can be built in heritage if the House understands why, chooses where and manages how it builds, and asks colleagues to walk collectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We can also build homes which are nestled in heritage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But we can do that if we understand collectively why we need to build, if we choose carefully where we build and if we manage carefully how we build.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And as we celebrate National Day, we will be going down to our estates as we usually do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: These estates were once upon a time, probably vegetated sites or brownfield sites, like Maju Forest was in 1976, but are now thriving estates with families, with homes, with generations raising families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, even as we have this very robust debate, can I ask my colleagues here in this House to walk with us collectively to assure our people that despite our limitations and our constraints, that we continue to shape our island into one of the most liveable cities in the world and with Singaporeans at the heart of everything we do.
